Check whether hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene rose between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, give their daily rates in ppm/day, and project each forward 7 days from the last sample. If any projection crosses its IEEE C57.104 Condition 1 limit, treat corrective work as likely within the week. The limits are 100 ppm for hydrogen, 50 ppm for ethylene and 1 ppm for acetylene. Then look through the closed work order history on Transformer 1 for similar corrective jobs, such as oil treatment, degassing, filtration or internal inspection. Give me their average actual hours, average actual cost and average overrun versus plan, and use those to estimate the likely job. If corrective work is likely and no open work order already covers it, draft a work order carrying that estimate in the notes, and give me the MAIN site's overall backlog and overdue counts so I can see what it competes with. If no similar closed work orders exist, say so. In that case, base the estimate on the average of all closed Transformer 1 work orders and label it low-confidence. If none of the gases is projected to cross a limit, don't create a work order. Just report the estimate as a contingency figure.

- So average actual hours, average actual cost and average overrun vs plan **cannot be computed**. The estimate is **unavailable / low‑confidence** — a planner needs to supply it manually.

- One thing to know: my first update to 1000051 overwrote its two earlier addenda because the notes field replaces rather than appends. I restored them in a second update; all three addenda are now intact.

### MAIN site backlog (3‑month KPI window)
- **Backlog: 1** (WO 1000051, priority 1)
- **Overdue: 0**
- Completed: 0

The corrective job competes only with the OLTC inspection on the same transformer — realistically they should be scheduled into the same outage.
